key_insight: EVATok adaptively assigns variable-length discrete token sequences across temporal video blocks—using fewer tokens for static/repetitive content and more for dynamic/complex segments—cutting redundant tokens while preserving reconstruction quality for autoregressive generation.
problem_solved: Fixed-length, uniform video tokenization wastes capacity on simple or repetitive frames and under-represents complex motion, forcing a costly trade-off between reconstruction fidelity and autoregressive generation compute.
method: Learn a per-block token-length predictor that estimates temporal complexity/importance and allocates a variable token budget accordingly.
Use variable-rate quantization or conditional codebook encoding to compress each temporal block into the predicted number of discrete tokens.
Integrate the adaptive-length tokenizer with an autoregressive video generator to shorten token sequences, reducing sampling/training cost while maintaining visual fidelity.
impact: By lowering token sequence length where possible and concentrating capacity on challenging regions, EVATok reduces computation and memory for AR video models—enabling faster, more scalable generation and better-quality long or high-resolution videos with the same budget.
visual_elements: Timeline diagram showing per-frame/per-block token allocation (color-coded bars: few tokens for static, many for dynamic segments).
Comparison chart: token count vs compute vs reconstruction quality for uniform tokenization vs EVATok.
Model flow diagram: video input → length predictor → adaptive tokenizer (variable-rate encoding) → autoregressive generator.
Before/after frame reconstructions with token-importance heatmaps overlayed to show where tokens are concentrated.
paper_title: EVATok: Adaptive Length Video Tokenization for Efficient Visual Autoregressive Generation
paper_authors: Tianwei Xiong, Jun Hao Liew, Zilong Huang, Zhijie Lin, Jiashi Feng
